To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the zebrafis ΔNp53 variant, which contains a truncated transactivation domain, is a potent developmental regulator and that its function is differentially regulated by the other p53 isoforms in developing zebifish.

the ΔNp53 protein antagonized the lethal effects of FL p53, and that ΔNp53 induced developmental defects that depended on p21 expression and were not counteracted when coexpressed with Δ113p53 in developing zebfish embryos.
ΔNp53 is differentially regulated from FLp53, and that the two N-terminal isoforms of p53 have differential functional effects in zebrafishes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the alternative p53 isoforms in development, and provides evidence for functional differences between the N-terminal p53 splice isoforms in vivo
the functional aspects of alternative N-terminal p73 isoforms in the developing zebrafisch embryos.
the functional consequences of coexpressing different zebrafish p53 isoforms in developing embryos.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zebrafich ΔNp53 is not a functional ortholog of Δ133p53.
Δ113p53 has a more proapoptotic and a less transactivatory function in comparison to ΔNp53.
the ΔN isoform of p53 is a dominant negative regulator of the wild-type p53 isoform in zebrafishes, and this is in contrast to the Δ113p53 which is not a dominant negative regulator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ΔNp53 variant has a more complex role in embryonal development and stress responses than the Δ113p53 variant.
the zebrafishes ΔNp53 variant, in contrast to the Δ113p53 variant, can functionally substitute for the full-length protein, at least to some extent.
the ΔNp53 is a dominant negative p53 isoform that is able to inhibit the activity of the FLp53 isoform, but that Δ113p53 does not have this ability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alternative N-terminal p63 isoforms have differential effects in zebrafishes, and that Δ113p53 and ΔNp53 have differential effects on p21 expression.
ΔNp53 is not a simple loss-of-function p53 variant, as has often been suggested in the literature.
the zebrafis ΔNp53 variant has distinct functional properties compared to the full-length isoform, and that it is a useful tool for dissecting p53 isoform-specific effects in a vertebrate model.
